newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Zairean embassy says no warrant out yet for Kengo.
newsitem.headline: Zairean embassy says no warrant out yet for Kengo.

text.p: Zaire's ambassador in Belgium said on Wednesday no arrest warrant had yet been issued for the African nation's former prime minister Kengo wa Dondo, who left his country for Switzerland.

Zaire's Information Minister Kin-Kiey Mulumba said on Tuesday an international warrant was being issued for Kengo's arrest after Zaire's new government had found the national treasury empty. Kengo was voted out of office three weeks ago.

"Up to this day, the Zairean government has not issued an international arrest warrant against the former prime minister, said a statement from the Zairean amabassador in Brussels, Kimbulu Moyanso wa Lokwa.
It was released through Belgian news agency Belga.

"It must be a question of an extrapolation of the government's decision to audit the companies which generate receipts that allow the state to meet its commitments, notably the payment of civil servants and the military," it added.
"This audit having been ordered on April 14, it seems to me premature to establish conclusions already."
The ambassador's statement said Kengo had not fled Zaire but left for Geneva "normally" by the international Ndjili airport outside Kinshasa on Sunday.

Swiss news agency ATS reported on Wednesday that Kengo had resurfaced in Geneva, where he said he was undergoing medical checks. The Swiss foreign ministry earlier confirmed he entered the country, though refused say whether he was still there.
The Belgium foreign ministry said it issued a new six-month visa to Kengo last week after his old one expired, but it did not know his current whereabouts.
Kengo, a part-Tutsi, had been widely accused of weakness in the face of a rebellion launched from eastern Zaire last October, initially by ethnic Tutsis. Rebels now hold about half the country.
